records.sourceFile: Using bar velocity to assess post-match neuromuscular fatigue in young soccer players.pdf

sourceVerification.doiVerification: DOI printed in the local PDF text.

records.evidenceSummary: Repeated-measures field study with 21 outfield U-19 male players (from 34 recruited) who played at least 60 minutes in one of three official matches. Countermovement jump, horizontal jump, and mean propulsive velocity in half-squat, bench press and hip-thrust (about 70% estimated 1RM) were measured before the match and at +30 min, +24 h and +48 h. The authors report that half-squat velocity fell 6.8% immediately after the match and recovered by 24 h, hip-thrust velocity remained reduced at 48 h, bench press was unchanged, and horizontal jump increased at 48 h.
records.limitations: The sample is small (21 players from two teams across three matches) and has 41 to 45% missing data at 24 h, with submaximal loads estimated rather than tested. Abstract and results do not fully agree (for example, the 24 h countermovement jump change and the 48 h hip-thrust change are reported differently), and the study measured external match load only.
records.synthesisCaution: Staff could take the hip-thrust finding as a general rule that posterior-chain training must wait 48 h after every match, when the study is a small single-cohort observation with missing data and mixed reporting of percentages.

changes: screeningLimitations: 'single team-season context' -> two teams across three matches ('from two teams competing'; 'Three official matches were analyzed (Team A, n=2; Team B, n=1)')
paper.tldr: bench press described as recovering faster -> it never declined ('Bar velocity in the bench press exercise did not differ from baseline values at any time point')

paper.athleteDev: advice to avoid hip-thrust as the first loaded lift is not supported (exercise order was not tested and hip-thrust was always performed last) -> caution on glute and hamstring loading at MD+1 and MD+2, as the authors recommend ('should be avoided at MD+1 and MD+2')
paper.limitations: added that reported percentages do not match the reported means ('0.67 +/- 0.09 vs. 0.64 +/- 0.09' reported as 6.8% in results and '5.05%' in discussion)
populations: removed Healthy Athletes because health status is not stated for the sample
verification.residualConcerns: Percent changes in the abstract, results and discussion are internally inconsistent with the reported means (CMJ at 24 h given as -1.7% though 39.58 to 36.67 cm is about -7%; hip-thrust at 48 h given as -7.4% though 0.62 to 0.58 m/s is about -6.5%). The extracted text also contains a second, tracked-changes copy of the manuscript with the same results.
